title: Senior's toolkit: a fast TDD loop
summary: Keep the red-green loop under ten seconds: dotnet watch, running one test, IDE shortcuts, golden masters with Verify, and small commits you can always go back to.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: the inner loop
steps.body: TDD only works when running the tests costs nothing. These keep the loop short, and give you an undo button.

toolkit.what: Rebuild and rerun the tests every time you save a file. Leave it running in a terminal beside the editor.
flags: watch only the tests you are working on

toolkit.what: Visual Studio: run the tests at the cursor (the test, class or file you are in) / run all tests. Rider and VS Code (C# Dev Kit) have the same commands: a run icon beside each test and a shortcut in their keymaps.
flags: Visual Studio: debug the test at the cursor
toolkit.example: Put the caret inside a [Fact], press Ctrl+R, T: only that test runs.

toolkit.what: Snapshot (golden master) tests with the Verify library (Verify.XunitV3): the first run writes a .received file, you approve it as .verified, later runs diff against it. Ideal for characterizing legacy output.
flags: committed with the code: the approved snapshot
the new output when it differs (do not commit)
not needed in current versions; the test returns Task

toolkit.what: Commit on every green. When a refactor goes wrong, you throw away two minutes of work instead of debugging it.
flags: drop the uncommitted mess, back to the last green
fold a tiny follow-up into the last commit
tidy the micro-commits before the pull request
toolkit.example:
git commit -am "green: custom separator"
# refactor goes badly
git restore .

steps.prompt: Match the situation to the tool.
pairs: you want the tests to run on every save
a refactor went wrong and you want the last green state back
you need to pin 200 lines of legacy report output
run only the test the caret is in (Visual Studio)

steps.prompt: A snapshot test fails after you changed the report's date format on purpose. What is the right move?
options: Read the diff between .received and .verified, and if the change is exactly what you intended, accept the new snapshot and commit it with the code
Delete the .verified file so the test passes
steps.explain: Snapshot tests make every output change visible. The review of the diff is the test: accept only what you meant to change, and the commit shows reviewers the new output.

steps.prompt: Watch only the Roman numeral tests while you work on them.
steps.explain: `dotnet watch test` reruns on save; arguments after `--` go to the test run, where xUnit's class filter takes wildcards.
